rows.title: `nuclear` — the command line of NuclearLang
rows.summary: NuclearLang: a minimal language for AI agents, transpiled to other technologies through declarative dialects (.nuc → .ts / .dart / .py). Commands: add, agent, analyze, ast, build, check, clean, code, contracts, credits, defs, device, dialect, doctor, explain, fix, fmt, gen, help, install, kind, make, migrate, monitor, new, packages, repair, run, setup, spec, terminal-device, test, tokens, watch.

--platform backend|mobile|web                               instead of --dialect: the platform's default dialect
(the Nuclear of a platform is the same in all of them)
--dialect-path <dir>   extra directory with dialects (repeatable; also $NUCLEAR_DIALECT_PATH, ':'-separated)
--defs-path <dir>      extra type definitions repository (repeatable; also $NUCLEAR_DEFS_PATH); the defs/
folder next to each dialects/ folder is always searched

rows.title: `nuclear-builder` — the Nuclear Builder without the editor
rows.summary: Sets up the AI services, keeps the software factory's teams and the providers' keys, runs a spec through the factory's stations with a team, retries a run, and exports the CI file.
body: ```text
nuclear-builder — the Nuclear Builder without the editor
nuclear-builder setup [--profile remote|lite|medium|hard] [--yes]
the AI services of this machine, step by step: it reads the hardware, suggests a
profile (which models are downloaded and how far each works), installs what is
missing (Ollama), downloads the models, loads the knowledge base and starts the
services, now and at every login (--yes: no questions, the suggested profile)
nuclear-builder setup --status [--json]      what is installed and running
nuclear-builder setup --clients              adds the MCP server to every AI client of this machine (Claude Code,
Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Gemini CLI): after installing a client
nuclear-builder setup --remove               takes the services away (Ollama, its models and the graph's data stay)
nuclear-builder setup --plan --json          this machine, the profiles and how each sits on it, the requirements
nuclear-builder setup --events --profile <id> [--from <step>]
the steps of a profile, one JSON line per event (what the editors draw)
nuclear-builder setup --restart graph|developer   a service again, through the system's manager
nuclear-builder setup --set KEY=value ...    writes the machine's choice (ai.env)
nuclear-builder team list|show <id>|save|delete <id>|default <id>|export <id> <file>|import <file>|roster [--lang en|es]|temperaments [--json]
the teams of the software factory (~/.config/nuclearlang/factory/teams): JSON on
stdout, an error as {"error": "..."} with exit code 1; `save` reads the team on stdin
nuclear-builder team screen [--lang en|es] [--json]
everything the company screen draws, in one call: {teams (as list), shown (each
team as show, or {error}), roster, temperaments, vault (as vault list, or null),
library and agents (as skills list, each with its markdown)}
nuclear-builder team create [--json]         a new team from the wizard's draft on stdin: {name, description,
purpose, skills, budgetUsd, techLead, logoFile, members: [{role, employee, kind,
provider, model, name}]} (who works a member not said: the local defaults)
nuclear-builder team suggest [--purpose <text>] [--skills a,b] [--lang en|es] [--limit <n>] [--json]
the employees of each role that fit the purpose and skills, each with why
nuclear-builder team name-suggest [--purpose <text>] [--lang en|es] [--json]
five satirical names for a team
nuclear-builder team runnable <id> [--json]  whether the team has a member of each role the project's stations need
nuclear-builder team update <id> [--name …] [--description …] [--purpose …] [--skills a,b] [--lead <member id>] [--budget <usd>] | duplicate <id> [--name …] [--json]
nuclear-builder team member add <id> --role <role> [--employee …] [--kind …] [--provider …] [--model …] [--name …] [--count <n>] [--json]
members hired (several: --count, or a JSON list of members on stdin without --role)

nuclear-builder team member remove <id> <member> | member update <id> <member> [--kind …] [--provider …] [--model …] [--employee …] [--name …] [--skills a,b] [--extra-skills <json>] [--instructions …] [--temperament …] [--gifs …] [--on …] [--note …] [--agent <library agent>] [--json]
a member let go, or changed (by its id in the team); who works a member is one
this machine has (agents --json), else it is refused with why
nuclear-builder team skills set <id> [--member <m>] --skills a,b [--json]
the library skills of the team (every member inherits them) or of a member
(beside its role skills switched on): skills list gives their ids
nuclear-builder team logo <id> <image> | logo <id> --clear [--json]
the team's logo: a .png, .svg or .jpg of 1 MB at most, copied beside the team as
<id>.logo.<kind>; --clear takes it away
nuclear-builder skills list [--team <id>] [--member <m>] [--lang en|es] [--json]
the library of skills and agents (nuclear-agents/skills, nuclear-agents/agents);
with a team, its skills and its own; with a member, its own, its base agent and
every skill it gets (composed: from library, team or member; what it overrides)
nuclear-builder skills show <id> [--team <id>] [--member <m>] [--lang en|es] [--json]
a skill's SKILL.md as that place sees it (the member's own, the team's own, the
library's, the role's), where it comes from and whether it can be changed there
nuclear-builder skills clone <id> --team <id> [--member <m>] [--json]
a copy of the skill as the team's own (every member inherits it) or the member's,
with the same id: it wins over the one it came from
nuclear-builder skills create|update <id>|delete <id> --team <id> [--member <m>] [--json]
an own skill of the team or the member: create and update read its SKILL.md on
stdin (front matter name, title, description, title_es, description_es, kind,
tags); a library skill is read-only (clone it to change it)
nuclear-builder vault set <provider> | remove <provider> | list [--json]
the API keys of anthropic, openai, google, openrouter in the system's keyring
(service nuclear-factory); `set` reads the key on stdin (asked for, hidden, in a
terminal), never from the command line
nuclear-builder run [spec.md] [--team <id>] [--events] [--confirm-spending] [--force-confirm]
the software factory: the spec through Analysis, Design, Tests first, Code,
Quality and Delivery, each station worked by its role as the team assigned it (no
file: the spec of specs/ changed last); it stops at the gates for you; --events:
JSON lines on stdout, the answers as JSON lines on stdin (what the editors use)
nuclear-builder run ... --detach             the run in a process of its own (no stdin: it waits at the first
question): {run, detached, log}; with a paid provider, waiting: spending
nuclear-builder run --resume <id>            a run that waits for you, from where it waits
nuclear-builder run answer <id> --answer approve|change|stop|yes|no [--text …] [--events] [--detach]
the answer to the question a run waits on (its process gets it, or the run goes
on with it); never the spending: that is confirmed twice where you answer
nuclear-builder run stop <id> | show <id> | journal <id>
a run's process stopped (a run that asks waits) · its file (JSON) · its journal
nuclear-builder retry <id> [--from <station>]   a run again from the station that failed (or --from that one)
nuclear-builder retry <id> --step <step>        a run again from one step (it and every step after it)
nuclear-builder restart <id>                 the whole run again: every file it wrote goes back first
nuclear-builder runs [--json]                the runs of this project

nuclear-builder metrics [--project <name|dir>] [--team <id>] [--member <id>] [--from YYYY-MM-DD] [--to YYYY-MM-DD] [--by day|week] [--view bill|throughput|cycle|burndown|flow|waiting|quality|people|indicators] [--json]
the reports of the factory from its ledger (~/.config/nuclearlang/factory/ledger), every
project of this machine: the bill (tokens in and out, USD, local against paid, the
budget used), throughput and velocity, cycle time, burndown, cumulative flow, the gates
waiting for you, quality, each member's work, the indicators (spec 017)
nuclear-builder checks <id> [list|on <check>|off <check>|add --title … --station … [--by user|role] [--prompt …]|mark <check> passed|failed|skipped] [--json]
the run's checks (checks.json in the spec's folder): QA's plan, yours
nuclear-builder spec new --title … --component <name>|_global [--layer presentation|domain|data] [--use-case …] [--description …] [--criteria …]... [--stdin] [--json]
the base of a spec in specs/<component>/[<layer>/]<id>/spec.md, with its acceptance
criteria (--criteria, repeated; --stdin: the whole markdown on stdin): {id, path, spec}
nuclear-builder spec show <id> | delete <id> [--json]
a spec's markdown, its draft and its run · its folder to .nuclear/builder/deleted/
nuclear-builder spec list [--json]           the specs by component and layer, with their runs
nuclear-builder spec move <id> --component … [--layer …] [--json]
a spec's folder to another component or layer (its run follows)
nuclear-builder spec migrate [--json]        the specs of the flat specs/<id>/ to their component
nuclear-builder spec accept <id> | discard <id> [--json]
a spec's draft (spec.draft.md, written by a member in Nuclear Chat) over the spec,
or thrown away
nuclear-builder member --team <id> --role analyst|architect|developer|qa|devops|chat --events [--root <dir>]
a member of a team answers once in Nuclear Chat (its responder): the conversation as
one JSON line on stdin ({member, channel, thread, messages, said, lang}), the answer
as JSON lines on stdout (typing, text, tool, ask, done); the role's provider with
the factory's tools, the spending confirmed twice; --role chat is the general agent

([--provider

] [--model ] [--kind …], the local Nuclear Developer by default)
nuclear-builder chat-host --json [--root <dir>] [--lang en|es]
the host file of Nuclear Chat for this project: the members of its team (the run's
team), their responders, the general agent `atlas` with its choices (the
agents below), the channels general and the team's
nuclear-builder agents [--json] [--root <dir>]
the agents that can answer a conversation on this machine: the local Nuclear
Developer (always), each agent whose command is on the PATH, each API provider with
a key in the vault ({id, kind, provider, label, models, defaultModel, available, why})
nuclear-builder models [--provider <id>] [--fresh] [--json] [--root <dir>]
the models of each provider that can work here (one when asked), from the provider:
Claude Code's aliases and ids, opencode models, an API's list (a key in the vault),
Ollama's installed models with their memory need and fit (fits, tight, too-big)
plus the small ones it can pull; and this machine's memory (lists kept 10 minutes)
nuclear-builder ci [check|test|security|artifacts|deploy ...]   the commands of .nuclear/builder.json
nuclear-builder export github|gitlab|bitbucket [--json]   writes the CI file that runs `nuclear-builder ci`
nuclear-builder line show | set KEY=<json> ...   the project's line (.nuclear/builder.json): read, or keys set
nuclear-builder connections [--team <id>] [--json]   Check the connections of a team
nuclear-builder read <path> [--json]         a file of the project as text (a PDF by pdftotext, a .pptx, markdown)
nuclear-builder mcp [--root <dir>] | mcp tools   the Builder's MCP server on stdio: every action above as a tool
(docs/02-architecture/actions.md) · its instructions and tools as JSON

rows.title: `nuclear-graph` — run, fill and guard the Nuclear Smart Graph
rows.summary: Runs the graph's server and its MCP server, builds and checks the knowledge base, ingests it, searches it, answers the exact questions and decides which programs may read it. Commands: serve, knowledge, ingest, search, answer, strategy, card, stats, connect, allow, deny, web-key, requests, revoke.
body: ```text
usage: nuclear-graph [-h]
{serve,knowledge,ingest,search,answer,strategy,card,stats,connect,allow,deny,web-key,requests,revoke} ...
`nuclear-graph`: run, fill and guard the Nuclear Smart Graph.
positional arguments:
{serve,knowledge,ingest,search,answer,strategy,card,stats,connect,allow,deny,web-key,requests,revoke}
serve               run the graph on 127.0.0.1 (NUCLEAR_GRAPH_PORT, default 7878)
knowledge           the knowledge base folder (nuclear-graph-storage/data): build its assets
from the working tree, check that they are what the tree gives now, record
the review of a hand-written row, ask the running graph the questions of
questions.toml and see that each finds its row, or compile every Nuclear
example of the hand-written rows
ingest              make the knowledge base folder what the graph knows (only what changed is
embedded again)
search              search the graph: by meaning and by exact name (a code, a command, a kind)
answer              what the graph gives for a question before a model answers it: the exact
facts of every question with one right answer it is (from the graph's
database), then the cards the shelves answer by meaning
strategy            which kind of request a text is (a whole system, one screen, a rename, a
failing test...) and its plan
card                one row of the knowledge base by its id (error:N0114,
kind:backend.usecase), with what it links to
stats               the rows of each collection and the revision of the knowledge base the
graph holds
connect             give a client (a program) access and keep its token in the keyring
allow               allow a pending request
deny                deny a pending request
web-key             keep the key of a search engine for the local agents (read from stdin):
brave
requests            pending access requests and the allowed clients
revoke              take a client's access away
options:
-h, --help            show this help message and exit
